subject: Future Tech
title: The Materials Explosion
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The Materials Explosion.

hook.text: Early 3D printers could only use brittle plastics.

buildup.text: Titanium, stainless steel, and nickel superalloys are now standard 3D printing materials used in aerospace and medicine.

discovery.text: Carbon fiber composites printed layer by layer can be stronger than aluminum at a fraction of the weight.

twist.text: Multi-material printers can mix different substances in a single object.

punchline.text: If you can melt it, dissolve it, or extrude it, you can print it.

quiz.question: Which composite material can be 3D-printed stronger than aluminum?
